faqHeading.title: Frequently asked questions.
faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for selecting the measurement, connection, reporting profile and platform integration.

faqs.question: Which pressure range should I choose for my installation?
paragraphs: Start with the normal operating pressure, the highest expected process pressure and any pump or valve transients. Published full-scale options are 1, 1.6, 3.5, 7, 10, 20, 35 and 100 MPa. Select a range that covers the process while providing the measurement performance you need around normal operation. Send those operating values with your enquiry so the range and any required pressure protection can be specified together.

faqs.question: Do I need gauge, absolute or differential pressure measurement?
paragraphs: Gauge pressure compares the process with local atmospheric pressure and is commonly used for water, air and hydraulic supply monitoring. Absolute pressure uses a vacuum reference. Differential pressure measures the difference between two points, such as across a filter. Tell us which reference your process requires, together with the range and application, so the appropriate sensing configuration can be confirmed.

faqs.question: Can I use the sensor with liquids, gases and my existing pressure port?
paragraphs: Suitability depends on the medium, its temperature, the wetted materials, seals and process connection. Share the liquid or gas, concentration where relevant, working temperature, port thread and available installation space. Hitelecom can then confirm a suitable configuration and connection. For viscous, crystallising or hygiene-sensitive media, include the cleaning method and any diaphragm or sanitary-connection requirement in the specification.

faqs.question: What does ±0.5% FS mean, and how is it different from annual stability?
paragraphs: FS means full scale. At ±0.5% FS, a 0–1 MPa range corresponds to ±0.005 MPa, while a 0–10 MPa range corresponds to ±0.05 MPa under the stated accuracy conditions. The published ±0.2% FS/year stability describes change over time; it is a separate specification. Compare accuracy, temperature conditions and the selected range against the smallest pressure change that matters to your application.

faqs.question: How should I choose between 4G, NB-IoT and LoRa?
paragraphs: Choose around coverage at the installed position, update requirements and your network ownership. For 4G or NB-IoT, confirm the operator service, supported bands and SIM arrangement. For LoRa, agree the gateway, protocol and platform path used by the supplied device. A commissioning check at the actual mounting location helps establish a practical reporting profile before wider deployment.

faqs.question: How should I set the sampling and reporting intervals?
paragraphs: Set sampling around the pressure changes you want to observe, and reporting around when the team needs to act. Share the normal process cycle, required alert timing and access for battery maintenance. The sensing workload, transmission frequency, signal conditions and temperature all affect the power plan. Hitelecom can help match the supported sampling and reporting settings to that operating profile.

faqs.question: What calibration information should I include in the project specification?
paragraphs: Specify the range, measurement reference, required acceptance tolerance and any certificate or traceability requirement. Set a verification schedule using the process importance, operating conditions, previous results and your quality system. For an existing installation, include recent comparison readings if available. Discuss the required test record and commissioning checks with Hitelecom so documentation can be agreed before delivery.

faqs.question: Can pressure readings and alerts connect to our own platform?
paragraphs: The published pressure-sensor specification uses MQTT, with reporting to Hitelecom Cloud, a customer cloud or a private platform. Share the destination, broker access requirements, device identifiers, pressure units and required alert rules. Agree the payload and the responsibility for evaluating thresholds, storing history and notifying users so the sensor data fits your existing workflow.

applications.title: Water Distribution Networks

image.name: water-distribution.webp
image.alt: Blue municipal water main in a concrete valve chamber, with a gate valve and capped isolated instrument branch.
image.caption: Application illustration: a service pressure connection beside a municipal main valve.

applications.tagline: See supply pressure by zone.
applications.description: Monitor pressure at district inlets, network branches and selected service points. A time-stamped pressure history helps water teams compare daytime demand, night-time operation and the effect of planned valve changes. Associate each sensor with its hydraulic zone and elevation, then review readings alongside pump status and the network records used to investigate supply concerns.
applications.objective: Understand pressure availability across selected supply zones.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved main or branch pressure tapping, connected through a service isolation valve.
applications.projectBrief: Network pressure envelope, installation elevation, water-contact materials, chamber exposure and reporting schedule.

applications.title: Booster Pump Stations

image.name: booster-stations.webp
image.alt: Bank of blue vertical booster pumps beside a stainless steel discharge header and valved instrument branch.
image.caption: Application illustration: monitor the selected booster-pump discharge header.

applications.tagline: Follow the pressure delivered by the pump station.
applications.description: Bring booster discharge pressure into the project dashboard for individual stations or a distributed pump estate. Readings show how delivered pressure changes with demand, pump staging and the selected operating schedule. Where the project needs suction and discharge information, define a measurement point for each side and review the pressure records together with the pump controller data.
applications.objective: Compare delivered pressure through demand and pump-staging changes.
applications.monitoringPoint: Approved pressure ports on the suction and discharge manifolds, as required by the project.
applications.projectBrief: Pump duty, suction and discharge ranges, manifold ports, operating temperature and the required observation interval.

applications.title: High-Rise Water Pressure Zones

image.name: high-rise-water.webp
image.alt: Domestic water manifold with stainless vertical risers, brass pressure-reducing assemblies and small pilot pipes.
image.caption: Application illustration: pressure observation within high-rise water supply zones.

applications.tagline: Keep each water-pressure zone in view.
applications.description: Monitor selected domestic-water risers, booster outlets and downstream pressure-reducing valve zones in high-rise buildings. Clear zone and floor identifiers make pressure history useful to facilities teams responding to service enquiries or checking a planned adjustment. Choose representative points within each zone and relate the readings to installation height, supply arrangements and periods of building demand.
applications.objective: Compare water-service pressure between defined building zones.
applications.monitoringPoint: A valved tapping on the zone manifold or an approved riser service connection.
applications.projectBrief: Building height and zones, expected pressure, connection access, potable-water requirements and plant-room coverage.

applications.title: Water Treatment & Backwash

image.name: water-treatment.webp
image.alt: Blue water-treatment filter vessels connected to a stainless manifold with small capped pressure service branches.
image.caption: Application illustration: selected pressure points around a treatment filter manifold.

applications.tagline: Put filtration pressure beside the operating stage.
applications.description: Monitor inlet and outlet pressure around selected filters or treatment stages. Readings taken in a defined operating state support comparison between filtration runs and planned backwash cycles. When both sides are instrumented, the project can calculate a pressure difference using matched readings and process context. Name each point by filter train and connection position so the history stays clear.
applications.objective: Compare pressure conditions across filtration runs and backwash cycles.
applications.monitoringPoint: Independent approved inlet and outlet pressure tappings on the selected filter train.
applications.projectBrief: Treatment stage, normal and backwash pressures, wetted materials, matching observation times and maintenance access; required pressure difference and combined measurement uncertainty.

applications.title: Wastewater Pump Discharge

image.name: wastewater-pumps.webp
image.alt: Green wastewater discharge pipeline with isolation and check valves and a raised isolated instrument connection.
image.caption: Application illustration: pressure observation on a wastewater discharge line.

applications.tagline: Know the discharge conditions at remote pump sites.
applications.description: Monitor discharge pressure at wastewater lift stations and transfer pumps to give maintenance teams a clearer record of each station’s operating conditions. Pair the pressure history with pump running status and known valve settings when reviewing a service event. Select a process connection suited to solids, fouling and cleaning access so the measurement point remains practical over the maintenance cycle.
applications.objective: Keep station discharge pressure alongside pump and valve operating records.
applications.monitoringPoint: A suitable discharge tapping with the selected diaphragm or process interface and service isolation.
applications.projectBrief: Effluent properties, solids content, pressure range, process interface, cleaning procedure and station environment.

applications.title: Fire-Water Pumps & Supply Lines

image.caption: Application illustration: remote pressure observation beside existing fire-water instruments.

applications.tagline: Keep test and maintenance pressure records accessible.
applications.description: Collect pressure readings from selected fire-water pump discharge and supply-line test points for facilities maintenance and scheduled checks. Identify the installation, test condition and observation period so technicians can compare like-for-like records over time. Integrate the monitoring data with the site maintenance workflow while retaining the approved fire-system controls and inspection procedures specified for the installation.
applications.objective: Document pressure during approved fire-water tests and maintenance.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved service pressure tapping on the pump discharge or designated supply-line test point.
applications.projectBrief: Approved connection, expected operating and test pressure, inspection workflow, observation interval and site requirements.

applications.tagline: See stored-air pressure through the production day.
applications.description: Monitor receiver outlet pressure to understand the air available to the factory as compressors load, unload and respond to demand. A clear pressure record helps utilities teams compare shifts, planned operating changes and machine-start periods. Match observations to compressor status and receiver identification, then choose a reporting profile that gives the required operating picture without collecting unnecessary updates.
applications.objective: See the receiver pressure available through compressor duty and production demand.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved receiver pressure port or a valved connection on the outlet manifold.
applications.projectBrief: Receiver operating pressure, air temperature, port specification, observation interval and plant communications.

applications.tagline: Compare air pressure where production uses it.
applications.description: Place measurement points on selected compressed-air branches and service drops to compare the pressure delivered around the factory. Review readings during known production states, especially where several lines share the same supply. Identify each sensor by distribution branch and location so utility teams can relate pressure changes to plant demand, valve changes and planned network work.
applications.objective: Understand compressed-air pressure availability at selected distribution points.
applications.monitoringPoint: A valved pressure tapping on the ring main, branch manifold or service drop.
applications.projectBrief: Branch locations, working pressure, production states, connection access and matching measurement schedules.

applications.title: Machine-Tool Air Supply

image.caption: Application illustration: monitor the air supply serving a machine tool.

applications.tagline: Bring the machine inlet into the pressure picture.
applications.description: Monitor air pressure at the approved service point feeding a machine-tool pneumatic circuit. The record gives technicians a reference for air supply during tool changes, cleaning operations and other defined machine states. Connect it with the machine identifier and relevant controller events so service teams can review what was delivered at the inlet when a supply question arose.
applications.objective: See inlet-air pressure during named machine operations.
applications.monitoringPoint: The approved air-preparation or inlet-manifold pressure port for the selected machine.
applications.projectBrief: Machine air requirement, regulator location, port approval, operating states and observation timing.

applications.title: Packaging-Line Pneumatics

image.alt: Carton packaging conveyor with pneumatic cylinder assemblies and a service-side air preparation block.
image.caption: Application illustration: observe regulated air supply at a packaging-line service point.

applications.tagline: Follow the air supply behind packaging operations.
applications.description: Monitor the regulated air feed to packaging equipment using the line’s approved pneumatic service point. Compare pressure records between production runs, product changeovers and simultaneous line operation. Keeping the measurement close to the selected manifold helps engineers understand the supply condition serving that section of the line and plan further investigation with the machine’s operating data.
applications.objective: Compare packaging-line supply pressure across runs and changeovers.
applications.monitoringPoint: The service pressure port on the regulated air manifold feeding the selected packaging section.
applications.projectBrief: Line sections, regulated pressure, machine cycle information, permitted connection and required sample interval.

applications.title: Pneumatic Clamping & Fixtures

image.caption: Application illustration: pressure observation at the air supply to clamping fixtures.

applications.tagline: Record the supply condition serving the fixture.
applications.description: Monitor regulated pneumatic pressure feeding an assembly clamp or fixture using its approved service port. Record the pressure in a defined held state or at the observation interval selected for the process, and keep the fixture identifier with each reading. The resulting history supports supply-pressure review during setup, product changes and planned fixture maintenance.
applications.objective: Confirm the recorded pneumatic supply condition for a defined fixture state.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved port on the fixture air regulator or supply manifold, outside moving tooling.
applications.projectBrief: Regulated pressure, held-state timing, fixture identification, port access and the process observation requirement.

applications.title: Air Dryers & Filter Stations

image.alt: Compressed-air filter station with two blue inline filters, refrigerated dryer and capped valved instrument branches.
image.caption: Application illustration: selected pressure connections around an air-treatment skid.

applications.tagline: Follow pressure through air-treatment equipment.
applications.description: Monitor pressure before and after selected dryers, filters or air-treatment assemblies. Compare readings under a known flow and operating condition, with point names that clearly identify the inlet and outlet. Matched observations support a project pressure-difference calculation and give utilities teams a useful operating record to review alongside service intervals, bypass settings and compressor data.
applications.objective: Compare treatment inlet and outlet pressure under the same operating conditions.
applications.monitoringPoint: Independent approved pressure ports on the selected treatment inlet and outlet manifolds.
applications.projectBrief: Air-treatment layout, pressure range, observation synchronisation, bypass states and service-access requirements; required pressure difference and combined measurement uncertainty.

applications.title: Injection-Moulding Hydraulic Units

image.name: injection-moulding.webp
image.alt: Injection-moulding machine service area with a hydraulic oil power unit, hoses and chained caps on test couplings.
image.caption: Application illustration: pressure observation from a hydraulic service manifold.

applications.tagline: Put hydraulic supply pressure beside machine operation.
applications.description: Monitor an approved pressure point on an injection-moulding machine’s hydraulic power unit or selected supply circuit. Periodic readings and defined hold-state observations create a pressure history for setup and maintenance review. Identify the circuit and machine state with the record, and specify the required measurement response where the project also needs detail from shorter process events.
applications.objective: Connect hydraulic-pressure records with the named circuit and machine state.
applications.monitoringPoint: A machine-approved hydraulic test port or rated manifold connection on the selected circuit.
applications.projectBrief: Machine and circuit, oil compatibility, pressure envelope, permitted test connection and measurement-response requirement.

applications.title: Metal-Forming Press Hydraulics

image.caption: Application illustration: a service pressure point outside the press tooling area.

applications.tagline: Review hydraulic pressure at a defined press state.
applications.description: Monitor a selected supply or hold-pressure point on a metal-forming press through an approved hydraulic connection. Keep the tooling setup and operating state with the pressure record so maintenance and production teams can make meaningful comparisons. Specify the observation timing around the process question, whether the project needs periodic operating records or a dedicated measurement arrangement for short events.
applications.objective: Compare hydraulic pressure for defined press setups and operating states.
applications.monitoringPoint: A rated press-manufacturer-approved test port or service manifold connection.
applications.projectBrief: Circuit pressure, fluid, tooling state, connection approval and the duration of the event to be observed.

applications.title: Machine-Tool Hydraulic Power Units

applications.description: Monitor the hydraulic supply serving machine-tool functions such as clamping, workholding or auxiliary actuation. A named circuit and defined observation state let technicians compare pressure history during setup and maintenance. Use the approved power-unit or manifold test point, and match the sensor range and fluid interface to the circuit rather than transferring a specification from another machine.
applications.objective: Keep the machine’s hydraulic supply pressure in the maintenance record.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved power-unit or service-manifold pressure test connection for the selected circuit.
applications.projectBrief: Machine circuit, fluid and temperature, pressure range, test-port fitting and operating-state definition.

applications.title: Hydraulic Lifts & Scissor Platforms

Record platform position, load condition and the selected circuit with the readings so comparisons have a clear context. Choose a protected service connection on the power unit or manifold and integrate the information into the equipment’s maintenance workflow.
applications.objective: Record hydraulic pressure with the platform position and load condition.
applications.monitoringPoint: A platform-approved hydraulic service port on the power unit or fixed manifold.
applications.projectBrief: Equipment approval, circuit range, fluid compatibility, load and position context, and service access.

Time-stamped readings help maintenance teams review the recorded supply condition during a known lubrication cycle and compare it with the controller’s operating record. Select the measurement interface for the lubricant’s viscosity and service temperature, and identify the pump or distribution section represented by the point.
applications.objective: Follow lubricant-supply pressure through the planned lubrication cycle.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved pressure port on the lubrication pump outlet or selected distribution manifold.
applications.projectBrief: Lubricant type and viscosity, pressure range, cycle timing, temperature and permitted process connection.

Define the test stage, hold duration and observation rate so the data answers the planned validation question. Associate each record with the assembly and test run, and select a suitable reference instrument and calibration arrangement for the acceptance criteria used by the engineering team.
applications.objective: Keep hydraulic test pressure linked to the component and test stage.
applications.monitoringPoint: A rated, supported instrument branch on the test manifold, with the selected fluid interface.
applications.projectBrief: Test pressure and hold time, oil and temperature, required uncertainty, reference method and data-export needs.

specifications.description: Published family values are a selection reference. Agree the range, pressure reference, medium compatibility and installed assembly in the supplied configuration. Environmental temperatures describe the equipment environment; process-medium temperature is reviewed separately.

rows.label: Available measuring ranges
rows.value: 0–1 / 0–1.6 / 0–3.5 / 0–7 / 0–10 / 0–20 / 0–35 / 0–100 MPa; select one range for the supplied configuration.

rows.label: Annual stability
rows.value: ±0.2% FS/year; a separate metric from measurement accuracy.

rows.label: Published overload limit
rows.value: ≤2 × full-scale pressure; specify expected process peaks with the selected range.

rows.label: Wireless options
rows.value: 4G Cat.1 / NB-IoT / LoRa, by model and supplied variant.

rows.label: Data protocol
rows.value: MQTT; agree the selected wireless data path and platform interface.

rows.label: Power and service-life profile
rows.value: Battery powered. Published design claim: more than 10 years at 1-hour reporting. Actual life depends on sensing workload, reporting, network conditions, temperature and battery configuration.

rows.label: Enclosure protection
rows.value: IP68 as listed in the family datasheet.

rows.label: Local configuration
rows.value: NFC activation, onboarding and maintenance configuration.

rows.label: Remote firmware service
rows.value: OTA upgrades via the configured platform.

rows.label: Housing installation
rows.value: Mounting lugs, pole clamp or slotted mount, by supplied configuration.

rows.label: Customization
rows.value: Measurement range, process thread, pressure probe, cable and wireless/reporting configuration on request.

sources.title: WIKA Handbook Pressure & Temperature Measurement
sources.evidence: PDFpages110–112 distinguish response time, full-scale accuracy and process/ambient/compensated temperatures; pages126–128 cover measuring-line arrangements.

sources.title: Find the right pressure sensor for your application
sources.evidence: Separate selections for media, technology, medium temperature, overload and hygienic uses show why one generic sensor cannot be assumed appropriate for every medium.

sources.title: PM15 with sanitary adapter system — installation guidelines
sources.evidence: Threaded process adapters, rated clamp/seal, specified tightening and atmospheric reference are installation-dependent. This describes ifm equipment, not an Hitelecom certification.

sources.title: Types of pressure: Absolute pressure, gauge pressure, differential pressure
sources.evidence: Gauge uses ambient reference, absolute uses vacuum reference, differential measures two pressurepoints; pressure type must match the task.

sources.title: WIKA USA Frequently asked questions
sources.evidence: Published manufacturer FAQ addresses pressure spikes, measurement accuracy, medium/temperature requirements, diaphragm seals and hazardous-area classification. It validates technical questions, not Hitelecom demand counts.

sources.title: Pressure gauge snubber — Model910.12
sources.evidence: Pressure pulsations and surges require suitable damping/protection; compresssors and hydraulic presses are named uses. Accessory availability/fit for Hitelecom must be separately specified.

sources.title: Pressure measurement — Endress+Hauser
sources.evidence: Diaphragm seals isolate aggressive/abrasive/viscous or hot/hygienic process media; complete assembly conditions influence accuracy.

sources.title: Pump monitoring with EdP transmitters
sources.evidence: Pump assessment uses pressure relationships and operating context; this supports pressure-monitoring relevance but does not prove single-point leak diagnosis or identical Hitelecom capability.

sources.title: USB pressure sensor — CPT2500
sources.evidence: Pressure-spike recording explicitly specifies time resolution and recording intervals. Other instruments’ fast response cannot be transferred to the HSeries.

sources.evidence: Vacuum, low-range and high-range work use different sensor variants, ranges and pressure connections. Standard positive MPa ranges do not automatically establish vacuum/differential capability.

sources.scope: Do not assert local operator coverage, roaming or power-saving functions without a deployment check.

sources.title: What is LoRaWAN Specification
sources.supports: A LoRaWAN gateway relays end-device messages to network-server infrastructure.

sources.title: Rosemount Wireless Pressure Gauge Reference Manual, May2025
sources.supports: High-refresh pressure-measurement mode draws battery power faster.
sources.scope: Engineering principle only; do not transfer Emerson's update intervals, network type or battery estimate.

sources.title: Calibration — National Physical Laboratory
sources.type: national metrology institute service and FAQ
sources.supports: Calibration compares measurement with a recognized standard; recalibration timing follows demonstrated needs and quality systems rather than one universal interval.
sources.scope: Supports maintenance topic; no assertion that Hitelecom is accredited or supplies a particular calibration certificate.
